intro: Welcome to the B2 passive! You already know 'is cleaned' and 'was built'. Now the passive goes into every tense and after modals (has been sent, is being fixed, must be finished), into the news style (It is said that…, He is believed to…), and you'll learn which verbs can never be passive and when the passive is the better choice.
teachingNotes: Recap in one line (B1 taught it): passive = be + third form (past participle), am/is/are and was/were, by + doer, used when the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant. New form rule: put be into the tense you need, then add the third form, which never changes: has/have been + third form (present perfect: Your order has been sent), am/is/are being + third form (present continuous: A new bridge is being built), was/were being + third form (past continuous: The room was being cleaned when I arrived), will be + third form (The winners will be announced on Friday; also is going to be announced), had been + third form (past perfect, mention only). Modals: must/should/can/could/may/might/have to + be + third form (The report must be finished today; Can it be paid by QRIS?; Phones mustn't be used). Memory trick: be after will/modals, been after has/have/had (sudah), being for the continuous (sedang).

Form errors to watch: *'The email has been send' → sent (the third form, not the base form; send → sent → sent); *'The report must be finish today' → must be finished: Indonesian 'harus diselesaikan' has di-, and di- = be + THIRD FORM, so both parts are needed; *'must finished' (no be); *'is been sent' / *'has being sent' (mixing been and being); *'is being build'; *'Your order been sent' (no has). Spelling: cancelled (British) / canceled (American); lift (British) = elevator (American).

Passive reporting (formal news style; Indonesian konon, dikabarkan, diperkirakan, diyakini, diduga): pattern 1 It + is + said/believed/thought/reported/expected/estimated/known + that + full clause (It is said that the house is haunted). Pattern 2 subject + is + said/believed/thought/reported/expected + to + base verb for now or the future (Prices are expected to rise; The house is said to be haunted), or to have + third form for something earlier (Pak Hasan is said to have moved to Bali). be shows when people said it (It was reported that…). No 'by people'. Errors: *'He is said that he is rich' (mixes the patterns), *'is reported to moved' / *'to has moved' → to have moved, *'is believed to leave last week' (earlier → to have left). Don't teach the continuous infinitive (is said to be working) or passive infinitive (is said to have been built) beyond one example if asked.

Intransitive verbs (no object) have no passive: happen, occur, take place, arrive, die, appear, disappear, rise, fall, exist. Indonesian trap: terjadi (ter- feels passive), tiba, meninggal, muncul, hilang, and diadakan (= was held, but take place has no object) → learners write *'The accident was happened', *'The flight was arrived', *'My grandfather was died', *'The event was taken place'. Test: can you say 'Someone [verb] it'? 'Someone stole my phone' ✓ → My phone was stolen; 'Someone happened the accident' ✗ → no passive. Contrast: kill has an object (Ten people were killed), be born is a fixed passive, raise has an object (Prices were raised) but rise doesn't (Prices rose; *'were risen').

Choosing active or passive (tendencies, not laws; only test clear cases): passive when the thing is the topic of the text, the doer is unknown/obvious/unimportant, and in formal, objective writing (reports, notices, news, academic texts, instructions, processes); active when the doer matters or is the news, in friendly chat and messages, and when the doer is I/we (I've sent the file, not 'The file has been sent by me'). If a passive names the doer, by + doer goes at the end, where English puts new, important information. In questions where both are grammatical, the task must say which form, tense or pattern to use.

Scope: no causative (have/get something done), no get-passive beyond recognising it as informal (My phone got stolen), no past modal passives (must have been done), no participle clauses. If asked, say they come in other lessons.

keyPoints.title: Every tense: be in that tense + third form
keyPoints.explanation: Put be into the tense you need, then add the third form, which never changes: has/have been sent (present perfect), is/are being built (present continuous), was/were being cleaned (past continuous), will be announced (future), had been sold (past perfect). After a modal, use be: must be finished, can be paid, should be signed, might be cancelled. Don't drop the helper or the third form: 'has been send' → has been sent, 'must be finish' → must be finished.

examples.en: A new bridge is being built over the river.
examples.id: Jembatan baru sedang dibangun di atas sungai.

examples.en: The report must be finished today.

id.title: Semua tense: be dalam tense itu + bentuk ketiga
id.explanation: Ubah be ke tense yang kamu perlukan, lalu tambahkan bentuk ketiga, yang tidak pernah berubah: has/have been sent (present perfect), is/are being built (present continuous), was/were being cleaned (past continuous), will be announced (future), had been sold (past perfect). Setelah modal, pakai be: must be finished, can be paid, should be signed, might be cancelled. Jangan buang kata bantunya atau bentuk ketiganya: 'has been send' → has been sent, 'must be finish' → must be finished.

keyPoints.title: News style: It is said that… / He is said to…
keyPoints.explanation: To report what people in general say or believe, without naming them: It + is said/believed/reported/expected + that + a full sentence, or person/thing + is said/believed/thought/expected + to + verb (now or future) or to have + third form (something earlier). It's formal, typical of news, like Indonesian konon, dikabarkan, diperkirakan, diyakini, diduga. Don't mix the patterns ('He is said that…') and never add 'by people'.

examples.en: It is said that this house is haunted.
Fuel prices are expected to rise next month.
examples.id: Harga BBM diperkirakan naik bulan depan.

examples.en: Pak Hasan is said to have moved to Bali.
examples.id: Konon Pak Hasan sudah pindah ke Bali.

id.title: Gaya berita: It is said that… / He is said to…
id.explanation: Untuk melaporkan apa yang dikatakan atau diyakini orang pada umumnya, tanpa menyebut siapa: It + is said/believed/reported/expected + that + kalimat lengkap, atau orang/benda + is said/believed/thought/expected + to + kata kerja (sekarang atau nanti) atau to have + bentuk ketiga (sesuatu yang lebih dulu). Gaya ini formal, khas berita, seperti konon, dikabarkan, diperkirakan, diyakini, diduga. Jangan campur kedua pola ('He is said that…') dan jangan tambahkan 'by people'.

keyPoints.title: Active or passive? And verbs with no passive
keyPoints.explanation: Choose the passive when the thing is your topic, when the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant, and in formal writing (reports, notices, news). Choose the active when the doer matters, in friendly messages, and when the doer is you. A verb without an object (happen, occur, take place, arrive, die, appear, disappear, rise) has no passive at all: 'The accident was happened' → The accident happened, even though Indonesian terjadi looks passive.

examples.en: Applications are reviewed within five working days.
examples.id: Lamaran ditinjau dalam lima hari kerja.
File-nya sudah saya kirim ke kamu.

id.title: Aktif atau pasif? Dan kata kerja yang tidak punya bentuk pasif
id.explanation: Pilih passive kalau bendanya yang jadi topik, kalau pelakunya tidak diketahui, sudah jelas atau tidak penting, dan dalam tulisan formal (laporan, pengumuman, berita). Pilih kalimat aktif kalau pelakunya penting, dalam pesan yang santai, dan kalau pelakunya kamu sendiri. Kata kerja tanpa objek (happen, occur, take place, arrive, die, appear, disappear, rise) sama sekali tidak punya bentuk pasif: 'The accident was happened' → The accident happened, walaupun 'terjadi' dalam bahasa Indonesia terlihat seperti pasif.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the present perfect passive of 'transfer': Good news, Rina: your salary ___ to your account.
assessment.rubric: Correct: has been transferred (present perfect passive: has + been + third form). 'has been transfer' = 40 (needs the third form). 'have been transferred' = 60 (salary is singular → has). 'has transferred' = 20 (active: the salary did the transferring). 'is been transferred' or 'has being transferred' = 30 (been after has; being is for the continuous). 'was transferred' = 50 (correct passive, but the task asks for the present perfect).

assessment.prompt: Complete with the present continuous passive of 'repair' (lift = elevator): Sorry, the lift ___ at the moment, so please use the stairs.
assessment.rubric: Correct: is being repaired (present continuous passive: is + being + third form). 'is repairing' = 20 (active: says the lift is repairing something). 'is been repaired' = 30 (been goes after has/have/had; the continuous needs being). 'is being repair' = 40 (needs the third form repaired). 'is repaired' = 40 (present simple: a routine, not happening now). 'has been repaired' = 30 (says the job is finished, but the lift can't be used now).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: All reports must be submit before Friday.
acceptableAnswers: all reports must be submitted before friday
all the reports must be submitted before friday
assessment.rubric: Correct: All reports must be submitted before Friday (modal + be + third form; Indonesian 'harus diserahkan': the di- needs be + submitted). 'must submitted' = 40 (be is missing). 'must be submitting' = 20. 'All reports must submit before Friday' = 20 (active: the reports can't submit anything). Spelling 'submited' = 80. Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Rewrite starting with 'It is said that': People say that this warung makes the best soto in Surabaya.
acceptableAnswers: it is said that this warung makes the best soto in surabaya
it's said that this warung makes the best soto in surabaya
it is said this warung makes the best soto in surabaya
assessment.rubric: Correct: It is said that this warung makes the best soto in Surabaya (It + is said + that + the same full sentence). Adding 'by people' = 70 (grammatical but unnatural: the point is that nobody in particular says it). 'It is said that this warung make…' = 70 (warung is singular → makes). 'It is said this warung to make…' = 20 (mixes the two patterns). 'It was said that…' = 60 (people say it now → is).

assessment.prompt: Rewrite starting with 'The new LRT line' (pattern: is expected to + verb): People expect that the new LRT line will open next year.
acceptableAnswers: the new lrt line is expected to open next year
assessment.rubric: Correct: The new LRT line is expected to open next year (subject + is expected + to + base verb for the future). 'is expected to will open' or 'is expected to opening' = 30 (after to, only the base form). 'is expected that it will open next year' = 30 (mixes the patterns: 'that' needs It at the start). 'is expected to be opened next year' = 90 (also correct, but the task asks for to + verb). 'is expecting to open' = 20 (active: the line expects).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: A serious accident was occurred on the Cipularang toll road last night.
acceptableAnswers: a serious accident occurred on the cipularang toll road last night
last night a serious accident occurred on the cipularang toll road
a serious accident happened on the cipularang toll road last night
assessment.rubric: Correct: A serious accident occurred on the Cipularang toll road last night (occur has no object, so it has no passive, even though Indonesian 'terjadi' looks passive). 'happened' instead of 'occurred' = 100. 'A serious accident occured…' = 80 (spelling: double r). 'A serious accident was occur…' = 10. 'A serious accident occurs…' = 50 (last night → past). Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: You're writing a formal news report and nobody knows who did it. Rewrite in the passive, without the doer, in the same tense: Someone has hacked the city council's website.
acceptableAnswers: the city council's website has been hacked
the city council's website's been hacked
the website of the city council has been hacked
assessment.rubric: Correct: The city council's website has been hacked (present perfect passive; the doer is unknown, so no by someone). '…has been hacked by someone' = 70 (grammatical, but by someone adds nothing and the task says without the doer). '…was hacked' = 60 (correct passive, but the task asks for the same tense, the present perfect). '…has been hack' = 40 (needs the third form). '…has hacked' = 20 (active: the website hacked something).

blocks.text:
Quick recap from B1: the passive is **be + the third form** (the past participle): *The office **is cleaned** every day. This house **was built** in 1990.* It starts with the thing that receives the action, and **by** (= oleh) names the doer when you need it.

Now the same idea works in **every tense**. The recipe:
- take the tense you need (present perfect, present continuous, future…),
- put **be** into that tense: **been** after has/have/had, **being** for the continuous, **be** after will,
- add the **third form**, which never changes.

Indonesian uses the same *di-* every time and adds a time word: *sudah dikirim*, *sedang diperbaiki*, *akan diumumkan*. English shows the time with the **helper verb** (has, is, was, will), so you can't drop it: 'Your order been sent' (no has) and 'A new bridge being built' (no is) are not complete sentences.

id.text:
Ringkasan dari B1: passive adalah **be + bentuk ketiga** (past participle): *The office **is cleaned** every day. This house **was built** in 1990.* Kalimatnya dimulai dengan benda yang dikenai tindakan, dan **by** (= oleh) menyebut pelakunya kalau perlu.

Sekarang ide yang sama berlaku di **semua tense**. Resepnya:
- ambil tense yang kamu perlukan (present perfect, present continuous, future…),
- ubah **be** ke tense itu: **been** setelah has/have/had, **being** untuk continuous, **be** setelah will,
- tambahkan **bentuk ketiga**, yang tidak pernah berubah.

Bahasa Indonesia memakai *di-* yang sama setiap kali lalu menambah kata keterangan waktu: *sudah dikirim*, *sedang diperbaiki*, *akan diumumkan*. Bahasa Inggris menunjukkan waktunya lewat **kata kerja bantu** (has, is, was, will), jadi kata itu tidak boleh dibuang: 'Your order been sent' (tanpa has) dan 'A new bridge being built' (tanpa is) bukan kalimat lengkap.

blocks.text: **been** or **being**? **been** comes after has/have/had (think *sudah*): *has **been** sent*. **being** is the -ing form (think *sedang*): *is **being** built*. 'is been sent' and 'has being sent' mix the two. And the last word is always the **third form**: 'The email has been send' → ***has been sent*** (send → sent → sent).

id.text: **been** atau **being**? **been** dipakai setelah has/have/had (ingat *sudah*): *has **been** sent*. **being** adalah bentuk -ing (ingat *sedang*): *is **being** built*. 'is been sent' dan 'has being sent' mencampur keduanya. Dan kata terakhirnya selalu **bentuk ketiga**: 'The email has been send' → ***has been sent*** (send → sent → sent).

blocks.prompt: The new MRT station ___ right now, so the road is closed.
blocks.explain: It's happening now and the station receives the action → present continuous passive: is + being + built. 'is building' says the station is building something, and 'has been built' says the work is already finished, which doesn't fit 'right now'.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: The new MRT station ___ right now, so the road is closed.
id.explain: Kejadiannya sedang berlangsung dan stasiunnya yang dikenai tindakan → present continuous passive: is + being + built. 'is building' berarti stasiunnya yang sedang membangun sesuatu, dan 'has been built' berarti pekerjaannya sudah selesai, tidak cocok dengan 'right now'.

material.title: Modals: must be done, can be paid

blocks.text:
A **modal** is a helper verb that adds meaning: *must* (harus), *should* (sebaiknya), *can* (bisa), *could*, *may* and *might* (mungkin), and also *have to* (harus). After a modal the verb is always in its base form, so the passive is **modal + be + third form**: *The report **must be finished** today.* (Laporannya harus diselesaikan hari ini.)

**The Indonesian trap:** in *harus diselesaikan*, the *di-* is exactly the part learners forget. 'The report **must be finish**' has be but no third form; 'The report **must finished**' has the third form but no be. Wherever Indonesian has *di-*, English needs **both**: be + finished.

Negatives put *not* after the modal: *Phones **must not be used** during the exam* (mustn't). Questions put the modal first: ***Can** the fee **be paid** by QRIS?*

id.text:
**Modal** adalah kata kerja bantu yang menambah makna: *must* (harus), *should* (sebaiknya), *can* (bisa), *could*, *may* dan *might* (mungkin), dan juga *have to* (harus). Setelah modal, kata kerjanya selalu dalam bentuk dasar, jadi passive-nya adalah **modal + be + bentuk ketiga**: *The report **must be finished** today.* (Laporannya harus diselesaikan hari ini.)

**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** dalam *harus diselesaikan*, bagian *di-* inilah yang sering dilupakan. 'The report **must be finish**' punya be tapi tidak punya bentuk ketiga; 'The report **must finished**' punya bentuk ketiga tapi tidak punya be. Setiap kali bahasa Indonesia memakai *di-*, bahasa Inggris perlu **dua-duanya**: be + finished.

Kalimat negatif menaruh *not* setelah modal: *Phones **must not be used** during the exam* (mustn't). Kalimat tanya menaruh modal di depan: ***Can** the fee **be paid** by QRIS?*

material.title: News style: It is said that… / He is said to…

blocks.text:
News and formal reports often tell you what **people in general** say, think or believe, without naming them. Indonesian uses *konon*, *dikabarkan*, *diperkirakan*, *diyakini*, *diduga*. English uses the passive of a **reporting verb** (a verb for saying or thinking: *say, believe, think, report, expect, estimate, know*). There are two patterns:

**1. It + is + third form + that + a full sentence**
*People say that this house is haunted* → ***It is said that** this house is haunted.*

**2. Person/thing + is + third form + to + verb**
*People say that this house is haunted* → *This house **is said to be** haunted.*
- **to + base verb** for now or the future: *Fuel prices **are expected to rise** next month.*
- **to have + third form** for something that happened **earlier**: *People say that Pak Hasan moved to Bali* → *Pak Hasan **is said to have moved** to Bali.*

No *by people*: the point is that nobody in particular said it. And **be** shows when people said it: *It **was** reported that…*, *She **was** thought to be…*

id.text:
Berita dan laporan formal sering menyampaikan apa yang dikatakan, dipikirkan atau diyakini **orang pada umumnya**, tanpa menyebut siapa. Bahasa Indonesia memakai *konon*, *dikabarkan*, *diperkirakan*, *diyakini*, *diduga*. Bahasa Inggris memakai bentuk pasif dari **reporting verb** (kata kerja untuk mengatakan atau berpikir: *say, believe, think, report, expect, estimate, know*). Ada dua pola:

**1. It + is + bentuk ketiga + that + kalimat lengkap**
*People say that this house is haunted* → ***It is said that** this house is haunted.*

**2. Orang/benda + is + bentuk ketiga + to + kata kerja**
*People say that this house is haunted* → *This house **is said to be** haunted.*
- **to + bentuk dasar** untuk sekarang atau nanti: *Fuel prices **are expected to rise** next month.*
- **to have + bentuk ketiga** untuk sesuatu yang terjadi **lebih dulu**: *People say that Pak Hasan moved to Bali* → *Pak Hasan **is said to have moved** to Bali.*

Tidak pakai *by people*: intinya memang tidak ada orang tertentu yang mengatakannya. Dan **be** menunjukkan kapan orang mengatakannya: *It **was** reported that…*, *She **was** thought to be…*

blocks.text: Two classic mistakes: 'He is said **that** he is rich' mixes the patterns → *It is said that he is rich* or *He is said to be rich*. And 'She is reported **to moved**' or '**to has moved**': after *to*, use the base form → *She is reported **to have moved***.

id.text: Dua kesalahan klasik: 'He is said **that** he is rich' mencampur kedua pola → *It is said that he is rich* atau *He is said to be rich*. Lalu 'She is reported **to moved**' atau '**to has moved**': setelah *to*, pakai bentuk dasar → *She is reported **to have moved***.

blocks.prompt: People believe that the painting is worth Rp5 billion. → The painting ___ worth Rp5 billion.
blocks.explain: Pattern 2: subject + is believed + to + base verb (the value is true now → to be). 'is believed that it is' mixes the patterns (that needs It at the start), and 'believes' is active: the painting doesn't believe anything.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: People believe that the painting is worth Rp5 billion. → The painting ___ worth Rp5 billion.
id.explain: Pola 2: subjek + is believed + to + bentuk dasar (nilainya berlaku sekarang → to be). 'is believed that it is' mencampur kedua pola (that perlu It di awal), dan 'believes' itu aktif: lukisannya tidak meyakini apa-apa.

id.title: Gaya berita: It is said that… / He is said to…

material.title: No object, no passive: happen, arrive, die

blocks.text:
Only verbs that **have an object** can be passive. The **object** is the person or thing that receives the action: *Someone stole **my phone*** → ***My phone** was stolen.* Some verbs never take an object: they're called **intransitive** (kata kerja tanpa objek). Nothing receives the action, so there's nothing to move to the front: **happen, occur, take place, arrive, die, appear, disappear, rise, fall, exist**.

**The Indonesian trap:** *terjadi* starts with *ter-*, which often feels passive (*tertulis, terjual*), and *diadakan* has *di-*, so learners add *was*: 'The accident **was happened**' ✗. English simply says ***The accident happened** yesterday.* The same goes for *tiba* (*The train **arrived** late*, not 'was arrived') and *meninggal* (*He **died** in 2015*, not 'was died').

Why is *was killed* fine, then? Because **kill** has an object: *The flood killed ten people* → *Ten people **were killed***. And *I was born* is a fixed passive you already know.

id.text:
Hanya kata kerja yang **punya objek** yang bisa dijadikan pasif. **Objek** adalah orang atau benda yang dikenai tindakan: *Someone stole **my phone*** → ***My phone** was stolen.* Ada kata kerja yang tidak pernah punya objek: namanya **intransitive** (kata kerja tanpa objek). Tidak ada yang dikenai tindakan, jadi tidak ada yang bisa dipindah ke depan: **happen, occur, take place, arrive, die, appear, disappear, rise, fall, exist**.

**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *terjadi* diawali *ter-*, yang sering terasa pasif (*tertulis, terjual*), dan *diadakan* memakai *di-*, jadi pelajar menambahkan *was*: 'The accident **was happened**' ✗. Bahasa Inggris cukup bilang ***The accident happened** yesterday.* Sama halnya dengan *tiba* (*The train **arrived** late*, bukan 'was arrived') dan *meninggal* (*He **died** in 2015*, bukan 'was died').

Lalu kenapa *was killed* boleh? Karena **kill** punya objek: *The flood killed ten people* → *Ten people **were killed***. Dan *I was born* adalah passive tetap yang sudah kamu kenal.

blocks.text: Quick test: can you say **'Someone [verb] it'**? *Someone stole my phone* ✓ → *My phone was stolen.* 'Someone happened the accident' ✗ → no passive: *The accident happened.*

id.text: Tes cepat: bisakah kamu bilang **'Someone [kata kerja] it'**? *Someone stole my phone* ✓ → *My phone was stolen.* 'Someone happened the accident' ✗ → tidak ada bentuk pasif: *The accident happened.*

blocks.prompt: My laptop ___ from my desk while I was at lunch.
blocks.explain: disappear (hilang) has no object: nobody 'disappears' a laptop, so there's no passive. 'was disappeared' and 'was disappear' add a be that English doesn't use here. (If you know someone took it, use steal: My laptop was stolen.)

id.prompt: Lengkapi: My laptop ___ from my desk while I was at lunch.
id.explain: disappear (hilang) tidak punya objek: tidak ada orang yang 'disappear' laptop, jadi tidak ada bentuk pasifnya. 'was disappeared' dan 'was disappear' menambahkan be yang tidak dipakai di sini. (Kalau kamu tahu ada yang mengambilnya, pakai steal: My laptop was stolen.)

id.title: Tanpa objek, tanpa pasif: happen, arrive, die

material.title: Active or passive? Choosing the better one

blocks.text:
Often both are correct English; the question is which one **fits**. These are tendencies, not strict laws.

**Choose the passive when…**
- the **thing** is your topic: a text about a museum keeps the museum as the subject (*The museum opened in 1975. It **has been renovated** twice.*)
- the doer is **unknown, obvious or unimportant**: *My account **has been blocked**.* *The road **is being widened**.*
- you want a **formal, objective** tone: reports, notices, news, academic writing and instructions (*Applications **are reviewed** within five working days.*)

**Choose the active when…**
- the doer **matters** or is the news: *Our team **won** the contract!*
- you're **chatting** or writing a friendly message: *We've fixed the bug!* sounds warmer than *The bug has been fixed.*
- the doer is **you**: *I've sent you the file* (not 'The file has been sent by me').

If a passive does name the doer, **by + doer** goes at the end, where English puts **new, important** information: *The new library was designed **by a young architect from Bandung**.* And remember: verbs with no object (happen, arrive…) give you no choice: active only.

id.text:
Sering kali dua-duanya benar; pertanyaannya, mana yang lebih **cocok**. Ini kecenderungan, bukan aturan mutlak.

**Pilih passive kalau…**
- **bendanya** adalah topikmu: teks tentang museum tetap menjadikan museum sebagai subjek (*The museum opened in 1975. It **has been renovated** twice.*)
- pelakunya **tidak diketahui, sudah jelas atau tidak penting**: *My account **has been blocked**.* *The road **is being widened**.*
- kamu ingin nada yang **formal dan objektif**: laporan, pengumuman, berita, tulisan akademik dan petunjuk (*Applications **are reviewed** within five working days.*)

**Pilih kalimat aktif kalau…**
- pelakunya **penting** atau justru itu beritanya: *Our team **won** the contract!*
- kamu sedang **ngobrol** atau menulis pesan yang santai: *We've fixed the bug!* terdengar lebih hangat daripada *The bug has been fixed.*
- pelakunya **kamu sendiri**: *I've sent you the file* (bukan 'The file has been sent by me').

Kalau kalimat passive memang menyebut pelakunya, **by + pelaku** ditaruh di akhir, tempat bahasa Inggris menaruh informasi yang **baru dan penting**: *The new library was designed **by a young architect from Bandung**.* Dan ingat: kata kerja tanpa objek (happen, arrive…) tidak memberi pilihan: hanya bentuk aktif.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is NOT natural English?
options: The report was written by me.
The report was written by the finance team.
blocks.explain: When the doer is you, English uses the active: I wrote the report. 'by me' sounds strange, even though Indonesian often says 'Laporannya saya tulis'. 'written by the finance team' is fine: the team is new, useful information at the end.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang TIDAK natural dalam bahasa Inggris?
id.explain: Kalau pelakunya kamu sendiri, bahasa Inggris memakai kalimat aktif: I wrote the report. 'by me' terdengar aneh, walaupun dalam bahasa Indonesia kita sering bilang 'Laporannya saya tulis'. 'written by the finance team' itu wajar: timnya adalah informasi baru yang berguna di akhir kalimat.

id.title: Aktif atau pasif? Memilih yang lebih tepat

id.intro: Selamat datang di passive level B2! Kamu sudah kenal 'is cleaned' dan 'was built'. Sekarang passive masuk ke semua tense dan dipakai setelah modal (has been sent, is being fixed, must be finished), ke gaya berita (It is said that…, He is believed to…), dan kamu akan belajar kata kerja mana yang tidak pernah bisa pasif serta kapan passive jadi pilihan yang lebih tepat.

assessment.bpas-1: Lengkapi dengan present perfect passive dari 'transfer': Good news, Rina: your salary ___ to your account.
assessment.bpas-2: Lengkapi dengan present continuous passive dari 'repair' (lift = elevator): Sorry, the lift ___ at the moment, so please use the stairs.
assessment.bpas-3: Perbaiki kesalahannya: All reports must be submit before Friday.
assessment.bpas-4: Tulis ulang dalam bahasa Inggris, diawali dengan 'It is said that': People say that this warung makes the best soto in Surabaya.
assessment.bpas-5: Tulis ulang dalam bahasa Inggris, diawali dengan 'The new LRT line' (pola: is expected to + kata kerja): People expect that the new LRT line will open next year.
assessment.bpas-6: Perbaiki kesalahannya: A serious accident was occurred on the Cipularang toll road last night.
assessment.bpas-7: Kamu sedang menulis berita formal dan tidak ada yang tahu siapa pelakunya. Tulis ulang dalam bentuk passive, tanpa pelakunya, dengan tense yang sama: Someone has hacked the city council's website.
